paper_title: Can LLMs Solve longer Math Word Problems Better
caption: : Gemini-Pro
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the informativeness scores of two methods, 0-CoT and CoRe, across five different points on the x-axis, labeled from 0 to 4. The x-axis is linear, ranging from 0 to 4 with integer tick marks at each unit. The y-axis, labeled "Informativeness," is also linear and ranges from 0.910 to 0.960, with tick marks at intervals of 0.010. The 0-CoT method is represented by a dashed blue line with circular markers, while the CoRe method is shown as a solid orange line with triangular markers. At x=0, the CoRe line starts at approximately 0.960, slightly above the 0-CoT line, which begins at about 0.958. As x increases, both lines show a consistent downward trend. At x=1, CoRe is at approximately 0.950 and 0-CoT is at about 0.952. At x=2, CoRe drops to roughly 0.933 and 0-CoT to about 0.935. At x=3, CoRe is at approximately 0.920 and 0-CoT at about 0.922. Finally, at x=4, CoRe ends at approximately 0.912 and 0-CoT at about 0.910. Throughout the entire range, the CoRe line remains slightly above the 0-CoT line, indicating consistently higher informativeness scores.
